_about: Episode 3 outline, scene level.  Each scene will be broken into beats (as in ep1) before its Fountain script is written.
title: The Secret Code of the MINIMOG

scenes._comment: Series main title, then this episode's subtitle; see titles/outline.json.
scenes.subtitle: sub.ep3

scenes.title: Twelve cells
scenes.summary: Ada keeps her promise not to memorize: she sends the twelve cards into Conway's 3 x 4 MINIMOG array.

scenes.title: A three-hour clock
scenes.summary: Arithmetic mod 3 on a clock with three hours. Sophie recognizes it: the diagonals that wrapped around in the kitten.

scenes.title: Nine words
scenes.summary: Choose a and b mod 3; the word is (b, a, a+b, a+2b). Nine words. Build the one for a = b = 1. Any two coordinates pin down the whole word: Ada's favorite property.
establishes: Any two coordinates determine a tetracode word

scenes.title: Odd man out
scenes.summary: Mark a hand in the grid. A column with one card gives its row; with two cards, the missing row; empty or full columns are wildcards. The rows must fit one tetracode word. Column counts 0, 1, 2, 3 are always rejected.

scenes.title: Test the hands
scenes.summary: The opening hand from Episode 1 reads 1, 1, 2, 2; the first two coordinates force 1, 1, 2, 0; the last disagrees, so it is not a hexad. The hand 1 to 6 is all wildcards: a hexad. Callback: the 24-hand Ada left Pascal in the worked game has the forbidden counts. The test is shown on examples; the paper proves it always agrees with the design.

scenes.title: Repair
scenes.summary: Which single exchanges turn the opening hand into a hexad? Six of them: three up (0 for 1, 2 for 10, 6 for 8) and three down (4 for 3, 7 for 5, 11 for 9). PASCAL: Seven for five. That was my move!

scenes.title: Signed patterns
scenes.summary: A brief look at signed patterns and the ternary Golay code behind the test. Cut if the episode runs long.

scenes.title: Why does it work?
scenes.summary: EULER: Repair the hand, then win. Every time. I want to know why. PASCAL: Who cares why? It works.
